disease_label_per_paper: Ochrobactrum anthropi catheter-related bloodstream infection in a hemodialysis patient
presentation_summary: 83-year-old hemodialysis patient with diabetes, end-stage kidney disease, and untreated multiple myeloma presented to the emergency department with fever 38.6 C.
He had a tunneled central venous catheter in the right internal jugular vein placed three months earlier for three-times-weekly hemodialysis.
He was hemodynamically and respiratory stable; catheter exit-site and tunnel exam were normal, and initial imaging did not reveal another focus.
Admission labs showed neutrophilia, CRP 37.3 mg/L, procalcitonin 1.2 ng/mL, anemia, and severe renal dysfunction.

actual_treatment.source_text_value: empiric intravenous amoxicillin-clavulanic acid dosage adapted to renal function
central venous catheter was removed the next day and replaced with a temporary hemodialysis catheter
targeted therapy with imipenem/cilastatin and ciprofloxacin for 14 days

outcome.source_text_value: condition improved, body temperature normalized, follow-up blood cultures were negative, and no recurrence occurred at 30 and 90 days

quality_warnings: Ochrobactrum species identity, DTTP, catheter-tip culture, susceptibility, and response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Presentation ranking uses tunneled central catheter, hemodialysis, malignancy/renal context, fever, lack of local tunnel signs as an observed negative, inflammatory markers, and renal labs.
